name: real_ikea_metod_60
description: Reference 'real' scene assembled from published product dimensions. No physical scene was captured; this file stands in for the capture step.

cabinet.product: IKEA METOD base cabinet frame 60x60x80 cm
cabinet.values: 600 x 600 x 800 mm, 18 mm panels, 80 mm legs

drawer.values: width 564 mm, depth 542 mm, side height 78 mm, max load 25 kg, full extension

worktop.values: depth 635 mm, thickness 28 mm; top surface at 80 + 800 + 28 = 908 mm above the floor

handle.values: length 143 mm, bar width 9 mm, projection 31 mm

drawer_pull_force.product: Custom Service Hardware full-extension soft-close slide (proxy; a different slide type)

friction.values: wood on wood 0.25-0.5, brick on wood 0.6

deviations: Robot frame: the Panda base is the origin and the counter top is at z = 0.30 m, i.e. the robot stands on a platform 0.608 m above the kitchen floor (908 mm worktop height).

Handle: the real handle is a horizontal bar with 31 mm projection. The skill API only allows top-down grasps, so the 143 mm bar is mounted vertically, 45 mm in front of the drawer front, and is 16 mm thick instead of 9 mm.
Drawer interior: modelled as 532 mm wide (564 mm minus 16 mm sides). IKEA does not publish the internal width; the Blum formula suggests about 489 mm.
Drawer travel: 0.50 m is an estimate for 'full extension' of a 542 mm drawer; no published figure.
Cup mass 0.13 kg is an estimate: only cup-plus-saucer mass (290 g) is published.
Cup shape: a scanned mug mesh (Google Scanned Objects) rescaled to the espresso cup's diameter and height.

Drawer friction and damping: no published opening force for this runner. frictionloss 2 N and damping 5 N s/m are placeholders, well below the 24-33 N of the proxy slide, so that the stiffened Panda gripper can pull the handle.
Gripper finger stiffness is 4x the Menagerie default (400 N/m) so that the grasp holds.
